upstreamNotes.note: Stage 4 constructs 'the skeletal filtration exact couple', but neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has a generic exact-couple notion at the pins (Mathlib has spectral objects and spectral sequences without exact couples), although the roadmap's inventory lists exact couples as a current Mathlib API. StableHomotopyKTheory:H.6/exact-couple plans the generic notion; stage 4's construction should instantiate it (or stage 4 should own the generic notion, in which case H.6 imports it).

Stage 2 item 6 (twisted singular chains) and stage 4 (cellular–singular comparison) do not state the cellular comparison with local coefficients, which homology of classifying spaces with local coefficients (Weibel IV 3.5.1, Whitehead VI.4.8) needs.

Stage 8 plans Kan homotopy groups but not Moore's theorem (homotopy groups of a simplicial abelian group are the homology of its normalised complex) nor Dold–Thom; both are needed to identify A[Sⁿ] with K(A, n).

sourceIssues.correction: whose n-simplices are chains of n composable morphisms X₀ → X₁ → ⋯ → X_n

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter IV, 2.9 The ℓ-adic completion, p. IV.22, in the author's chapter file Kbook.IV.pdf (SHA-256 9f1c1b8c…)
sourceIssues.printed: The source identifies K₁(C; Z_ℓ) = π₁(K(C); Z_ℓ) with Z_ℓ.
sourceIssues.correction: By the formula of 2.9, π_n(E; ℤ_ℓ) is an extension of T_ℓ π_{n−1}(E) by the ℓ-adic completion of π_n(E); for E = K(ℂ), n = 1: K₁(ℂ) = ℂ^× is divisible, so its completion vanishes, and T_ℓ K₀(ℂ) = T_ℓ ℤ = 0; hence K₁(ℂ; ℤ_ℓ) = 0 and the Tate module ℤ_ℓ of ℂ^× appears in K₂(ℂ; ℤ_ℓ).
sourceIssues.reason: Direct application of the extension stated in the same paragraph; recorded in the reviewed decomposition (REVIEW-EXT-01-EXT-15) and re-checked here.
searched: Weibel's K-book errata page (https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook.html, list of corrections; not reachable for a full check in this run)

sourceIssues.locator: Appendix C, Definition C.4, p. 162, in arXiv:1707.01799
sourceIssues.correction: For a covariant X : I → Top and strings i₀ → ⋯ → i_n the coefficient is X(i₀) (or the strings are written in the opposite direction).
sourceIssues.reason: With X(i_n) the last face map d_n, which drops i_n, would need a map X(i_n) → X(i_{n−1}) against the arrow; the formula as printed is the one for contravariant diagrams.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 1.7, p. V.8, in the author's chapter file Kbook.V.pdf (SHA-256 52dcc8ee…)
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims equivalence with E(B, Sn f, Sn C), the category of extensions of B by Sn C. It gives |wS.B| → |wS.(Sn f.)| → |wS.(Sn C)| and takes Xn = |wS.B| for every n.
sourceIssues.correction: S_n f is equivalent to the extension category E(C, S_n f, S_n B) of S_n B by C, and the degreewise split fibrations are |wS.C| → |wS.(S_n f)| → |wS.(S_n B)|, with X_n = |wS.C|; their realisation is the sequence Ω|wS.(S.B)| → |wS.C| → |wS.(S.f)| → |wS.(S.B)| that the proposition states.
sourceIssues.reason: By IV.8.5.3, S_n f = S_n B ×_{S_n C} S_{n+1} C contains C as the objects (0, C = ⋯ = C) and projects exactly onto S_n B, so the sub term is C and the quotient term S_n B; with the printed roles the realisation would have |wS.B| as its second term, contradicting the statement.

sourceIssues.locator: §2, paragraph before Definition 2.1, p. IV.18, and proof of Proposition 2.7, p. IV.21, in Kbook.IV.pdf (SHA-256 9f1c1b8c…)
sourceIssues.printed: The source characterizes it by the vanishing of all reduced integral homology groups except H̃ m (P ) = Z/ℓ.
sourceIssues.correction: P^m(ℤ/ℓ) = S^{m−1} ∪_ℓ e^m has only one nonzero reduced integral homology group, H̃_{m−1}(P) = ℤ/ℓ (and H̃_{m−1}(P) = ℤ/q₁ × ℤ/q₂ in the proof of Proposition 2.7).
sourceIssues.reason: The same sentence defines P^m(ℤ/ℓ) by attaching an m-cell to S^{m−1} by a degree-ℓ map; its cellular chain complex ℤ →ℓ ℤ in degrees m and m − 1 has homology ℤ/ℓ in degree m − 1 and 0 in degree m (ℓ ≥ 1).

sourceIssues.locator: Exercise 1.1, second paragraph, p. IV.14, in Kbook.IV.pdf (SHA-256 9f1c1b8c…)
sourceIssues.printed: The source asks for the conclusion that the canonical S 3 → X + map gives a homotopy equivalence.
sourceIssues.correction: X⁺ is homotopy equivalent to S³ (by the first part of the exercise there is a homotopy equivalence S³ → X⁺), but the canonical composite S³ → X = S³/Γ → X⁺ is not one: equivalently, the degree-one map X → S³ collapsing the complement of a ball is a plus construction.
sourceIssues.reason: S³ → S³/Γ is a 120-sheeted covering of closed oriented 3-manifolds, of degree 120 on H₃, and X → X⁺ is an isomorphism on H₃; so the composite multiplies H₃ ≅ ℤ by 120.
